nodes.action: skipped the flaky tests to make CI green
the regression reached every user and forced a full rollback
ran the full regression suite before release
added a feature-flag rollback switch to limit exposure if one slipped through

traffic hit a cluster that could not serve it

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Morning, Dev. You see the CI status this morning?

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Yeah, red again. Those three flaky tests in the payments module keep failing on the runner.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I skipped them to get the pipeline green. We needed a clean build for the release candidate.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Skipped? That feels risky. Those tests cover the refund edge cases.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I know, but they're flaky, not failing. I'll re-run them locally after the release. We can't block the train on noise.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Alright, but if something slips through, that's on us.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: It won't. The full regression suite passed last week. We're good.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Melanie, we have a problem. The refund calculation regression just hit production.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: What? How? We ran the full regression suite before release.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Apparently the flaky tests we skipped were the ones that would have caught it. It's reached every user now.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Damn. We're doing a full rollback. I'm on it.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Rollback is already in progress. But this is bad — every single user got the wrong refund amount for the last hour.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I hear you. I'm adding a feature-flag rollback switch to the refund service so if anything like this slips through again, we can kill it instantly without a full deploy.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Good. But also, we need to stop skipping tests.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Agreed. No more skipping. Full suite, every time.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Hey, I saw you pointed DNS at the new cluster this morning. Did you check the health endpoint first?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Actually, I did wait for the cluster health check this time. Last week I pointed DNS before it was ready and traffic hit a cluster that couldn't serve it. That was a mess.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Yeah, I remember. But this time it went smoothly?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Traffic moved over without a hitch. The health check passed, and we're serving from the new cluster now.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Nice. And the regression from last week — did the full suite catch anything new?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: That's the thing. We ran the full regression suite before the last release, and it still didn't catch the refund bug because it took so long that we cut corners on timing. Turns out that wasn't enough.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: So what are you doing differently?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I was wrong about the full suite being the safety net. We replaced it with parallel execution and a fast critical path — the high-risk flows run first, in parallel, so we get results in minutes instead of hours. The full suite still runs, but it's not the gate.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: That makes sense. So the critical path catches regressions before shipping, and the full suite is just a slower backstop.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Exactly. And with the feature-flag switch, even if something slips through, we can contain it to a small percentage of users. No more full rollbacks.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Good. Let's hope we don't need it.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Fingers crossed, but now we're prepared either way.
